rules.sentence: In contrast to maternal ITP, gestational thrombocytopenia rarely brings the count below 70,000/dL, typically does not cause bleeding, and has its origins in a dilutional, not consumptive, mechanism.[3]

Neonatal alloimmune thrombocytopenia may occur in pregnant women who are negative for the platelet antigen PL a1 but were sensitized in prior pregnancies by infants who were PL a1 positive or by blood transfusion.
Pregnant women with ITP have an increased incidence of fetal loss, a low fetal birth rate, and a higher incidence of premature births.[3]
In drug-induced ITP, the drug absorbs the platelet cell membrane.
The immune system makes antibodies to the target drug-platelet complex, which results in the removal of the sensitized platelet by phagocytes residing in the spleen and liver.
The activation of the complement system by the classical pathway is another effector mechanism of platelet cell damage (thrombocytopenia).[7]
